notes: PSI lists three of the six flights: Saffire-I (PSI-98), Saffire-II (PSI-99) and Saffire-III (PSI-100). Saffire-IV, -V and -VI had no PSI record in the search dump of 2026-11-14 (psi-access.md), so their psi_id and psi_url are null and their records rest on NTRS papers and NASA pages.

Full texts were fetched for this file and saved under raw/pdf/<ntrs id>.pdf with pdftotext -layout output as .txt: 20210011521, 20240002981, 20260001992, 20170008805, 20180005168, 20200000557, 20170000230, 20170001636, 20210017343, 20220002714, 20240008602, 20250002675, 20260001600, 20150022421, 20210017785. PSI documents saved there too: PSI-98/99/100 Operations PDFs and the two Readme .docx files (text extracted from word/document.xml).

Quotes with source.kind 'pdf' come from pdftotext -layout output. Quotes that are table rows are copied as the row appears in that text (cells separated by spaces); the claim spells out which column is which, read from the table header in the same file.

Source conflict, Saffire-III flow speed: PSI-100 text and its Experimental table say 30 cm/s; the NTRS slides (20180005168) and the 2021 flight paper (20210011521, Table 2) say 25 cm/s. Both are recorded; SAFFIRE findings on Saffire-III name which source they use.

Source conflict, Saffire-II flow speed: the PSI-99 Experimental table lists 20 cm/s for all nine samples and the PSI text says 'either 20 or 30 cm/s'; the NTRS slides (20170008805) say 20 cm/s for all tests except sample 2-6 at 25 cm/s.

Source conflict, Saffire-I/III radiometers and igniter: PSI text says two radiometers and the PSI table gives 182 W ignition power; the NTRS slides (20170008805) say four radiometers and list 165 W in one slide and 182 W in the results table.

Source conflict, Saffire-V atmosphere: the NASA Saffire page says samples were burned at 8.2 psia and 34% oxygen; the flight paper (20210011521, Table 1) tabulates 70.7 to 72.6 kPa and 25.4 to 26.2 mol % for the three burns; the rib paper (20210017785) gives 761 hPa and 26.9 vol % for sample V-4. Findings use the per-test values of the paper they quote.

Source conflict, Saffire IV-VI values between the 2024 paper (20240002981) and the 2026 paper (20260001992): e.g. VI-3 peak heat release 3080 W vs 3240 W, CO increase 308 vs 338 ppm, and IV-1 oxygen 22.0 mol % vs 0.23 mol fraction. The 2024 paper is marked preliminary; each finding quotes one paper and keeps that paper's numbers.

Source conflict, dates: PSI-98 gives investigation dates 03-02-2001 to 02-28-2008, which do not match the 2016 flight; years here follow the NASA news release and fact sheet. The NASA fact sheet says Saffire-IV launched on Northrop Grumman CRS-15 while the flight paper says Saffire IV and V flew on NG-13 and NG-14, and the NASA page says Saffire-V launched on CRS-14. The 2026 paper states the series 'began in 2017 with SAFFIRE I through III occurring between 2017 and 2019', against 2016-2017 in the NASA pages and NTRS slides.

Sample width for Saffire-VI is 41 cm in the 2024 abstract and 40 cm in the 2026 paper. PSI-98 table columns label 40.6 as length and 94 as width; the PSI text and the NTRS slides give 0.94 m long by 0.4 m wide.

Saffire has no test of an extinguishing agent: its suppression evidence is about ventilation (stopping, reducing and restoring airflow). No smoke particle size distribution numbers beyond 'submicron (PM1) dominated' and 'larger particles (dp > 4 um) for PMMA' are in the saved Saffire texts. The presentation 20210017343 is a slide deck whose two-column layout breaks some sentences in the extracted text; only lines that survive intact were quoted. No partial-gravity test exists in this family; the 2024 paper says so itself (SAFFIRE finding on partial gravity).

Findings attached to one flight sometimes rest on a statement covering several flights (for example Saffire I and III, or IV and V); the claim names the flights. Findings from normal-gravity support tests (silicone pre-flight tests, low-pressure PMMA tests) are filed under Saffire-II, the flight they were run for, with evidence_level 'normal-gravity test' or 'model or analysis'.

The 2018 abstract's phrase 'consumed 1.5 of the available oxygen' (20170008805) has lost its unit in NTRS and was left out. The NTRS record 20210012108 (Combustion Product Monitor) has no PDF download; only its abstract was used, for instrument context.

Source conflict, flow direction: the 2026 paper's Table 1 caption says 'All samples were 40 cm wide in 20 cm/s opposed flow', while the 2021 and 2024 papers tabulate the flat PMMA and fabric burns as concurrent (only the structured V-4 sample as opposed). Conditions here follow the 2021 and 2024 tables.
decision_hint and earth_instinct are interpretation written for VESTA, not NASA statements.
